question: After civil-war poachers killed most of Gorongosa's elephants for ivory, why were so many young females born tuskless?
options: Stress made adults shed their tusks
Mothers taught calves to break tusks
Tuskless survivors passed the trait on
answer: Tuskless survivors passed the trait on. Poachers ignored elephants with no ivory, so those lived and bred. Campbell-Staton and colleagues found tuskless females rose from about 18% to about 51% and traced the trait to genes on the X chromosome. Nobody chose tusklessness; guns kept choosing against its opposite.
move: Ask who was removed from a group before explaining how it changed.
ask: Which habits around me spread simply because the alternatives kept being removed?
trap: Hardship seems to change bodies directly, and the young then inherit it.
reference: Campbell-Staton et al., Ivory poaching and the rapid evolution of tusklessness in African elephants, Science, 2021
